title: The gap between max yield and current yield is pre-authorized discretionary headroom for the vault operator
content:
Each Spark Savings v2 risk block records two yield figures rather than one: a `Max yield` and a `Current yield (at launch)`. The recorded pairs are 10% / 0% for Avalanche USDC (A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.3.4.2.1.4.2.1), 6% / 3.2% for Robinhood Chain USDG (A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.3.5.1.1.4.2.1), and 6% / 0% for X Layer USDT (A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.3.6.1.1.4.2.1).

Governance therefore approves a **band**, not a rate. Everything between launch and the ceiling is delegated to the setter role.

The rationale is competitive: savings rates must respond to market conditions on a timescale far shorter than a governance cycle, and an instance launched at 0% is a live venue awaiting demand rather than a mispriced one. The ceiling caps the worst case — the maximum liability Sky can accrue per unit of deposit — while leaving the operating point to whoever is watching the market.

The corresponding cost is that the Artifact's stated yields become stale immediately. A reader cannot infer Sky's current cost of funds from the Atlas; only the ceiling is authoritative, and the two numbers can diverge arbitrarily far within the band without any recorded governance event.
description: Instances launch below their governed ceiling — USDG at 3.2% against a 6% max, USDC and USDT at 0% against 10% and 6% — letting rates be moved competitively without a new governance vote.
